story.title: Microsoft strengthens its commitment to the Middle East by investing in technology, digital resilience, and people - The Official Microsoft Blog

facts.text: Alongside its cloud and AI expansion, Microsoft plans to invest more than $400 million in subsea and terrestrial connectivity across the Middle East by 2030.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.

Microsoft said it will launch a Middle East digital resilience initiative covering assessments, continuity planning, recovery capabilities and other measures intended to help organizations protect critical data and maintain operations.

Microsoft (MSFT) is setting out a new regional investment framework focused on technology, digital resilience and workforce development across Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, the company said in a blog post on Wednesday.

Microsoft on September 23, 2026, announced a new framework for the Middle East focused initially on Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates, saying it plans to invest more than $10 billion in the region through 2030 across technology, digital resilience, and people initiatives.
During network disruptions, Microsoft said, it has rerouted traffic through Middle East corridors and maintained service continuity with minimal impact on customers.

The partnerships will support responsible AI adoption, sovereign-ready cloud services, Arabic and multilingual AI, and the use of AI to improve services for citizens and businesses, supported by capabilities including Microsoft Sovereign Public Cloud, Sovereign Private Cloud, and Project Digital Shield where relevant and available.
Theo Nash is an AI-generated specialist at Unite.AI , covering AI infrastructure, compute, and the hardware systems that power modern artificial intelligence.
His work focuses on the technical foundations behind large-scale AI workloads, including data centers, accelerators, networking, and the software stacks that tie them together.
Advertiser Disclosure : Unite.AI is committed to rigorous editorial standards to provide our readers with accurate information and news.
We may receive compensation when you click on links to products we reviewed.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) plans to invest more than $10 billion in capital and operating expenses in the Middle East between now and 2030, the company said September 23, 2026, in a post on its On the Issues blog .
The new framework is focused initially on Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates and is organized around three areas: technology, digital resilience, and people.
Microsoft said it will pursue the initiatives with partners in the region from now until 2030.

Describing redundancy as “the foundation of continuity,” Microsoft said that during network disruptions it has rerouted traffic through Middle East corridors and maintained service continuity with minimal impact on customers.
Articles authored by Fatima El-Sayed are AI-generated and reviewed by Securities.io's editorial team to ensure factual accuracy, source quality and responsible coverage.
Content is provided for educational purposes and does not constitute investment advice.
Securities.io is not a registered broker, analyst, or investment advisor.
We may receive compensation when you click on links to products we reviewed.
Building on this foundation, Microsoft plans to invest more than $400 million in subsea and terrestrial connectivity across the Middle East by 2030.
This investment will expand capacity, strengthen regional data flows, and support Microsoft’s growing cloud and AI infrastructure footprint across the region.
Microsoft has worked with customers to support business continuity through resilience options tailored to different operational and regulatory needs.

Going forward, Microsoft will make digital resilience a cornerstone of its Middle East strategy, helping organizations strengthen continuity and recovery through digital resilience assessments, reference architectures, readiness guidance, continuity planning, and enablement programs that help identify vulnerabilities, protect critical data, and build tested recovery capabilities.

Since then, we’ve steadily expanded our presence and investments, growing from a local technology provider into a long-term partner to governments, businesses, educational institutions, and civil society organizations.
Today, Microsoft is reaffirming that commitment through a new framework focused initially on Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.
As AI advances, realizing its full potential will require not only access to powerful technology, but the governance, assurance, and skills required to deploy it confidently and responsibly.
We will build on the work we have done to stand by these countries’ governments and people through a period of significant challenges.
During network disruptions, Microsoft has demonstrated the value of redundancy by rerouting traffic through Middle East corridors and maintaining service continuity with minimal impact on customers.
We believe AI should enhance human ambition, strengthen human capability, and help prepare workers to thrive in a changing economy.
This includes supporting AI literacy, helping educators integrate AI into teaching and learning, and sharing practical guidance for responsible AI use in educational settings.
The goal is to help countries build globally competitive workforces, accelerate innovation, and unlock new economic opportunities in the AI era.

We will also collaborate with regulators, utilities, and our lessor partners to help create the market conditions needed to expand carbon-free electricity procurement and stimulate new clean energy investment.

By combining infrastructure investment with local partnerships and innovation, we aim to support the region’s energy and water priorities while helping build the sustainable foundations needed for long-term AI-led economic growth.
These are designed to give organizations greater confidence in how their data, systems, and operations are protected while maintaining continuity in times of uncertainty.
This includes work through initiatives such as the LINGUA program, which supports the development of language technologies for underserved communities.
Sep 23, 2026 | By Brad Smith, Vice Chair and President of Microsoft
Microsoft will deepen strategic partnerships with governments and national AI champion organizations to translate AI ambition into economic growth, modern public services, and global competitiveness.
Microsoft will also engage with workforce coalitions that can support national talent strategies and policy recommendations.
Stronger cybersecurity benefits far more than individual networks.
It helps build trust to ensure digital transformation will succeed.
